doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sidemen in the Snookum Russell and Carter bands; Max and Miles; four trombones
summary: Johnson recalls Carter band players, including Porter Kilbert and Bumps Myers, meeting Max Roach, and a four-trombone section.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who were some of the other people who were with Snookum Russell at the same time you were?
Unfortunately, Lida, Fats is the only one I remember by name. I’m sorry about that, but I don’t remember the other band members. I don’t remember their names.
Who all was in the Benny Carter Orchestra with you that you remember?
A few names come to mind if I try hard. There was the alto saxophonist, whose name was Porter Kilbert.
Lord have mercy.

There was a tenor saxophone player whose name was Bumps Myers. The lead trombonist, a wonderful lead trombonist, a little dude. In order to be seen he had to sit on a stack of telephone books in the orchestra. What was his name? [John "Shorty" Haughton] He was a wonderful player. He could do the Tommy Dorsey style approach to ballads beautifully. I can’t think of his name.
I know it and can’t think of it either.
Yeah, you'd know him.
Yeah.
Oh, he had it down, that articulate vibrato in the high register. It was wonderful. It was beautiful. And Max [Roach]. We’re still talking about Benny Carter?
Uh huh.
Max played drums with Benny Carter for a very short time, in addition to George Russell.
And that was when you met Max, also?
My best recollection is [that's] when I first met Max. Miles played with Benny Carter for a hot minute.
Really?

Somewhere along the line. I wish I could be more accurate chronologically about when that happened, but it’s documented somewhere. I read it, even. I recall it, but I don’t know if I was there when Miles was with Benny Carter. Who else was with Benny at that time? I wish I could think of the other, because it was a good trombone section. [Possibly Alton Moore and John "Shorty" Haughton] I enjoyed that trombone section. The bass player, Charles Drayton. Bass player, Charles Drayton.

We can actually look on the [album cover], 'cause we have the album from it. [It] says simply Benny Carter 1944. There’s a picture of you in the trombone section. Fact is, in this particular picture there were four trombones.
Oh, wow, yeah.
That was really unusual.
Yeah, Benny was a four trombone leader for a while.
Yeah.
It was economics, obviously. To have four trombones was a luxury in those days unless you were Basie or Lunceford or Duke or what not. But, yeah.
